thread:
mike: Heads-up — saw an 8-12% p95 regression on host ingress for short-turn chat (seq < 64) after last night's kernel-selector rollout.
anya: Which pools/hosts?
mike: host-group-2 and host-group-5. Canary pool has the largest delta.
cheng: Any profiles?
perf-bot: uploaded profile: gs://perf-artifacts/1763828888/ingress-flame-2026-03-22.html
perf-bot: quick summary: host-ingress CPU +13% vs baseline; kvcache miss rate +35% for small payloads; syscall writev spike correlated with frequent small writes. Hot stacks: parse_stream -> tokenize_chunk -> kv_cache_lookup -> grpc_writev.
sam: paste top stack snippet?
mike: snippet:
```
parse_stream()
  -> tokenize_chunk()
  -> kv_cache_lookup() [hot]
  -> grpc_writev()
```
anya: kvcache miss spike could be normalization/routing change. Kernel-selector v2 went out last night.
cheng: did a curl microbench across seq sizes. median latency 12ms -> 14ms for seq=32; p95 25ms -> 28ms. Looks like batching forms smaller batches; preparse seems stalling some inflight requests.
mike: hypothesis: selector change altered preparse timing, triggering extra memcpys / smallwrites and earlier writev syscalls. That raises syscall overhead and fragments batching windows.
anya: plan: A/B rollback kernel-selector on a canary pool and try toggling prefix normalization.
sam: quick dev run disabling prefix normalization: p95 for seq<64 improved ~9%. Command:
```
bench/ingress_micro --clients=200 --seq=32 --mode=http2 --iter=2000
```
cheng: instrumented kvcache with normalized-key tags on dev. Found many keys with leading NUL in some payloads — normalization not stripping control char.
mike: if keys differ by leading NUL we get miss amplification; explains +35% misses.
anya: rolling back selector on canary (host-group-2) now.
perf-bot: deploy rollback initiated: kernel-selector v2 -> v1 (canary). start 2026-03-22T14:40:00Z; watch 15m.
sam: I have a small writev coalesce patch in my branch — reduces writev syscall count by ~22% locally. PR WIP: https://github.com/redwood/infer/pull/1456
cheng: added kvcache normalized-key logging. sample:
[2026-03-22T14:12:01Z] key_in: "\u0000user:abc" normalized: "user:abc" hit:false
[2026-03-22T14:12:01Z] key_in: "user:xyz" normalized: "user:xyz" hit:true
mike: great catch. If normalization bug is root cause we can hotfix normalization and re-enable selector.
anya: rollback complete on canary at 2026-03-22T14:50:05Z. Canary p95 back to baseline after ~10m. Keeping rolled back until fixes land.
mike: action items:
- anya: keep selector rolled back cluster-wide for now
- cheng: land kvcache normalization fix + unit/integration tests
- sam: land writev coalesce + run 1h canary stress
- mike: add perf dashboard for seq<64 and auto-alert on kvcache miss delta
sam: will open final PR and run canary stress when merged.
cheng: will add unit tests for normalization and a small e2e kvcache test.
perf-bot: suppressed perf alerts while rollback is active.
mike: I'll write a short postmortem + rollout plan. Let's not flip selector until normalization and coalescing validated. Thanks all :thumbsup:
